verdict_basis: R1-R9 and N1-N4 are resolved. NEW-1 (high) and NEW-2 (medium) from round 3 are only partially resolved. This head adds two high, one medium and one low new source finding. Cold re-evaluation of unreceipted facts can drop already-applied irreversible revocations. The release linkage gate checks binary names that do not exist. This is a scoped static review. Execution evidence names 06869b6 and e3d240e, not this head. It is not repository or release acceptance.

evidence: ensure_removal_rotations now rotates again when the current generation's wraps contain any fingerprint in facts.removed_members, even if per-target bookkeeping is complete. The concurrent_rotations_cannot_leave_removed_device_in_current_wraps test covers rotation arriving before facts.

The unsafe-current check reads only fact-derived removed_members. A peer-authored, validated `member.remove` commit marks a member removed in the folded document, but it never enters facts.removed_members and never appears in the facts.jsonl removal loop. No rekey happens, and later writes under the generation that still wraps that device are accepted.

author_commit is not an independent guard. After ensure_removal_rotations it checks only generation_id == dek.current, never that the current wraps exclude every removed member. Any path where the repair loop does not rotate (commit-based removal, `continue` on an unparsable record, or NEW-3 ordering) still admits writes under an unsafe generation.
The test calls ensure_removal_rotations directly. It does not assert that a write is refused before re-rotation.
resolution_conditions: In author_commit, refuse secret.put_version with team_rekey_pending whenever dek.generations[current].wraps contains any member whose folded status is not active. Use the folded document, not only the facts overlay.
Include member.remove commit removals in the repair trigger, or reject member.remove ops.
Add a test that writes before repair is refused, plus a commit-based removal variant.

new_findings.title: Unreceipted facts are re-judged against current authority, so cold load can permanently drop already-applied irreversible revocations
evidence: For a line with no local receipt, load_facts checks fact_role_ok against fold(all current commits, facts accepted earlier in the file), not against authority at admission time.
Every line written before this build has no receipt. The same applies to a missing or replaced fact_admissions.json.

Example: admin X authored a connection_disabled or secret_version_revoked fact that was accepted and applied. Later X is demoted (member.set_role commit) or removed by a member.remove commit. Commits are not ordered relative to fact lines, so both changes are present in every prefix fold.

On the next load_environment or register_env, X's earlier fact is quarantined and facts.jsonl is rewritten. The fact overlay loses it, so derive_local can re-activate the connection or version locally.
Peers still hold the fact and replay it, but validate_incoming_fact against the current document rejects it again, so the divergence is permanent.
This contradicts team-sync §7.4: facts are monotone and cannot be undone.
The same rule also discards historic incident facts whose author is no longer active.
resolution_conditions: Never quarantine a line that was previously applied. For example, add a one-time signed migration receipt for all existing lines on first load by this build, and keep receipts durable and outside restore.

Alternatively, evaluate cold lines only for member_removed under the existing reciprocal rules, and never retract connection_disabled or secret_version_revoked facts that pass signature checks from an author who was an admin at any point in signed history.
Add tests: an unreceipted disable or revoke followed by demotion via member.set_role commit, and removal via member.remove commit. Assert the fact survives restart and the connection stays disabled.

new_findings.title: Local authors do not observe received HLCs, so a repair rotation can sort before the unsafe generation it is meant to replace
evidence: author_commit builds Hlc::new(0,0), observes only this author's previous commit, then ticks the wall clock. handle_commit and submit_commit never advance env.hlc from received commits.
A peer rotation with an HLC up to MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS (5 minutes) ahead is accepted, not deferred. A deferred one is released later at its future HLC.
If that rotation's generation still wraps a removed device, ensure_removal_rotations' new rotation sorts earlier, so dek.current does not change.
author_commit then accepts writes prepared under the unsafe current generation (generation_id == current). Each write call creates another rotation commit until wall time passes the peer HLC.
This contradicts §5.2: work authored after observing another commit always sorts later.
resolution_conditions: Before ticking in author_commit and TeamSync, observe the maximum HLC in the store, including released deferred commits.
After a repair rotation, assert the new generation became current. Otherwise fail closed with team_rekey_pending.
Add a test with a peer rotation up to 4 minutes ahead.

new_findings.title: State lock held across network I/O, and receipt bookkeeping is quadratic
evidence: handle_fact and publish_fact now hold StateDir::lock, an exclusive flock shared with the admin CLI and every state writer, through refold, broadcast, and send_removal_notice session.send calls. A slow or blocked peer send stalls all local state transactions.
store_fact also calls receipt_fact, which unwraps the device key through KMS, while holding the envs mutex.
fact_admissions.json is rewritten in full for every admitted fact, so cost grows with the square of the fact count.
Each unreceipted cold line triggers a full fold.
Durability ordering is safe: the receipt is written before the line append, and the rewrite uses tmp+fsync+rename. Neither fsyncs the parent directory.
resolution_conditions: Release the state lock before broadcast and notices.
Load the device key outside the envs mutex.
Bound or append-structure the receipt store.
Optionally fsync the parent directory after renames.

non_findings_checked: Lock ordering is consistent: state lock before the envs mutex in store_fact, quarantine_local_fact, refold and handle_fact. No path takes the state lock while holding envs. Re-entrant nested locks in author_fact, load_facts and receipt_fact are safe per the supplied store.rs.

Admission receipts are Ed25519 signatures by the local device key over a domain-separated {env_id, hash}. Without the KMS-wrapped key they cannot be forged by writing the receipts file. A non-object receipts document falls back to the cold check.
ensure_removal_rotations reads the raw removal lines after load_facts has quarantined unauthorized ones, so unauthorized removals no longer drive rekeying.
rotate_dek_bound issues a dek.rotate op with no secret.put_version, so author_commit does not recurse into ensure_removal_rotations.
build-release.py still verifies the source SHA-256 before extraction, rejects unsafe archive members and rebuilds the SDK every run.
limitations: Static review only. Nothing was built, executed or installed, and the file hashes were not checked against 9a9f007.
